items.headline: Gurvinder Pal Singh sworn in as Delhi High Court judge; working strength reaches 50
items.text: Judicial officer Gurvinder Pal Singh took oath as an Additional Judge of the Delhi High Court on 7 October. Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre administered the oath. His appointment followed the Supreme Court Collegium's recommendation in September and the Centre's notification earlier this month.
items.why: The court now has 50 working judges against a sanctioned strength of 60, leaving 10 posts vacant.

items.headline: Supreme Court asks Delhi High Court why so many execution petitions are pending
items.text: A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran asked the Delhi High Court to explain its unusually high pendency of execution petitions. The matter arises from the Supreme Court's earlier direction that all High Courts clear pending execution petitions within six months. The court noted that about 2 lakh such petitions were disposed of across High Courts in the last six months, but about 8.8 lakh are still pending, with Maharashtra alone accounting for over 3.4 lakh.
items.why: Execution petitions are how people actually get what a civil decree awards them, so delays here leave court wins unenforced.

items.headline: CJI to examine plea to recall split verdict on Election Commissioners' appointment law
items.text: An application was mentioned before Chief Justice Surya Kant seeking recall of the 23 September split verdict on the 2023 law on appointing the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. It says Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, one of the two judges, did not disclose that his son is standing counsel for the Election Commission. The CJI agreed to examine it; a separate curative petition raises the same ground.
items.why: The plea raises the question of when a judge must disclose a possible conflict of interest and step aside from a case.

items.headline: 281 lawyers apply for Senior Advocate designation under Madras High Court's new rules
items.text: In the first round under its 2026 designation rules, the Madras High Court received 281 applications for Senior Advocate designation. The court published the list of applicants on 6 October and will accept views from the Bar on them until 27 October. The new rules, notified in July 2026, replaced the old 100-point scoring system, following a May 2025 Supreme Court judgment.
items.why: This is the first test of the new system, which assesses ability, standing and professional ethics instead of awarding points.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 6 October to 10:00 AM IST, 7 October 2026

items.headline: Former CJI BR Gavai and two retired judges criticise Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's public remarks on voter-roll revision
items.text: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai said judicial propriety would not allow him to comment on a matter that is pending before the courts, and stressed that sitting judges should avoid speaking publicly on pending cases. Retired Delhi High Court judges SN Dhingra and RS Sodhi also criticised Justice Bhuyan's address at NALSAR on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, an issue still being heard by the Supreme Court.
items.why: The exchange revives the debate over how far sitting judges may speak in public on issues that are sub judice.

edition.window: News from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM IST, 6 October 2026

items.headline: Three High Court Chief Justices take oath as Supreme Court judges; strength rises to 37
items.text: Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh were sworn in as judges of the Supreme Court at an afternoon ceremony, with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant administering the oath. They were until now the Chief Justices of the Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana High Courts respectively. The Court's working strength, including the CJI, goes up from 34 to 37 against a sanctioned strength of 38.
items.why: With Justice Agarwal's elevation the Supreme Court has three sitting women judges, and only one vacancy is left.

items.headline: Delhi High Court bids farewell to Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya
items.text: The Delhi High Court held a full-court farewell reference for Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya on his elevation to the Supreme Court, attended by the court's judges, government counsel and members of the Bar. He said that where the law could not deliver a just outcome he had 'tried to softly bend the law towards justice', and described the Delhi High Court's mix of cases as unparalleled. Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, who now heads the court, spoke of his administrative and collegial approach.
items.why: The Delhi High Court will function under an Acting Chief Justice until a permanent appointment is made.

items.headline: CJI Surya Kant says compassion, not only efficiency, must govern court proceedings
items.text: Delivering the second Prof. (Dr.) N.R. Madhava Menon Memorial Lecture, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant repeated his line that algorithms may schedule hearings but compassion must govern proceedings. He said compassionate judging means looking at the whole human context of a case rather than legal abstractions, and set out five questions for courts, including how unheard victims are treated and how compassion can be built into legal aid and courtroom procedure. He also called for closer work between the judiciary and legal academia.

items.headline: Delhi High Court's new Senior Advocate designation rules take over from the 2024 framework
items.text: The Delhi High Court Designation of Senior Advocate Rules, 2026 replace the rules notified in 2024 and reset how the court confers the senior gown. An applicant must ordinarily have ten years of practice and be 40 years of age, subject to the exceptions written into the rules, and the designation is decided by the Full Court after assessment and voting. The rules also set out the application route and the evaluation parameters.
items.why: Senior designation decides who can appear as lead counsel, so the eligibility and voting rules matter to the whole Bar in Delhi.

items.body: National Law University and Judicial Academy, Assam
items.headline: NLUJA Assam to hold its fourth convocation on 10 October in Guwahati
items.text: The National Law University and Judicial Academy, Assam will hold its fourth convocation on 10 October at the Sri Sri Damodardeva International Auditorium in Guwahati. Supreme Court judge Justice Vikram Nath will be the chief guest and Justice Ujjal Bhuyan the guest of honour, with Gauhati High Court Chief Justice Ashutosh Kumar, the university's Chancellor, also present. In all 107 graduands and scholars will receive degrees: 53 from the five-year B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) course, 48 from the one-year LL.M. and six Ph.D. scholars.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 5 October to 10:00 AM IST, 6 October 2026

items.body: Delhi High Court / Ministry of Law and Justice
items.headline: Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre named Acting Chief Justice of Delhi High Court
items.text: The Centre has notified Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre as Acting Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court under Article 223 of the Constitution. He will carry out the Chief Justice's duties once Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya leaves office on his elevation to the Supreme Court.
items.why: Delhi High Court will be led by an acting head until a regular Chief Justice is appointed.

items.body: Gujarat High Court / Ministry of Law and Justice
items.headline: Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak named Acting Chief Justice of Gujarat High Court
items.text: The Centre has notified Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak to perform the duties of Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court under Article 223. The appointment follows the elevation of Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal to the Supreme Court, notified the same day.

items.body: Telangana High Court / Ministry of Law and Justice
items.headline: Justice P Sam Koshy named Acting Chief Justice of Telangana High Court
items.text: The Centre has notified Justice Puthichira Sam Koshy as Acting Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court under Article 223. He takes charge once Chief Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh relinquishes office on his elevation to the Supreme Court.

items.headline: Outgoing Gujarat Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal urges women lawyers not to let others' doubts limit them
items.text: At her farewell reference before moving to the Supreme Court, Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal told young women lawyers not to let circumstances or other people's doubts set the limits of what they achieve. She asked senior women in the profession to mentor newcomers and said integrity, hard work and humility build a lasting reputation at the Bar.

items.headline: Election Commission says Bihar SIR order was a unanimous decision upheld by Supreme Court
items.text: Responding to allegations by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, the Election Commission said its June 2025 order for the Special Intensive Revision of Bihar's voter rolls was approved unanimously by the full Commission. It pointed out that the Supreme Court upheld the exercise in May 2026; separate petitions questioning alleged unilateral decisions by the Chief Election Commissioner, including changes to Form 6, remain pending.

edition.window: News from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM IST, 5 October 2026

items.body: Ministry of Law and Justice / Supreme Court of India
items.headline: Centre notifies three High Court Chief Justices as new Supreme Court judges
items.text: The Central Government on Monday notified the appointment of Chief Justices Sunita Agarwal (Gujarat), D.K. Upadhyaya (Delhi) and Aparesh Kumar Singh (Telangana) as judges of the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended their elevation on 28 September.
items.why: The Supreme Court will now have 37 judges against a sanctioned strength of 38, and the Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana High Courts will need new Chief Justices.

items.headline: Five Additional Judges of Andhra Pradesh High Court made permanent
items.text: The Law Ministry has notified the appointment of five Additional Judges of the Andhra Pradesh High Court as permanent judges: Justices Maheswara Rao Kuncheam, Thoota Chandra Dhana Sekar, Challa Gunaranjan, Avadhanam Hari Haranadha Sarma and Dr. Yadavalli Lakshmana Rao. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended this last month.

items.headline: Justice Kaushik Goswami appointed permanent judge of Gauhati High Court
items.text: The Centre has notified Additional Judge Kaushik Goswami as a permanent judge of the Gauhati High Court, following the Collegium's recommendation of 23 September. He was a Senior Advocate and Standing Counsel for the High Court before becoming an Additional Judge in November 2023.

items.headline: Justice Subhash Upadhyay appointed permanent judge of Uttarakhand High Court
items.text: The Centre has notified Additional Judge Subhash Upadhyay as a permanent judge of the Uttarakhand High Court, on the Collegium's recommendation of 23 September. He served as Standing Counsel for the State from 2012 and became an Additional Judge in May 2025.

items.body: Gujarat High Court Advocates' Association / Bar Council of Gujarat
items.headline: Gujarat lawyers strike over Rent Bill; Advocate General says it will not become law
items.text: Lawyers in Gujarat, including the Gujarat High Court Advocates' Association, stayed away from court work on 5 October against the Gujarat Rent Bill, 2026, which would move rent disputes from courts to revenue officers. In the High Court, Advocate General Kamal Trivedi said the Government had assured the Bar Council that the Governor would not sign the Bill and that it 'will not see the light of the day'.
items.why: The Bill has passed the Assembly; the assurance suggests the State may restore the earlier law that keeps rent disputes with the courts.

items.headline: NUSRL Ranchi women students protest over campus safety and hostel rules
items.text: Women students at the National University of Study and Research in Law, Ranchi, held a night-time protest and gave the administration a list of 14 concerns, including poor lighting, missing CCTV, staff entering the girls' hostel without notice and stricter exit rules for women. Reports say the issues are now being resolved internally.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 4 October to 10:00 AM IST, 5 October 2026

items.headline: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan: any process that disenfranchises millions of voters is arbitrary
items.text: Speaking at the valedictory of the 19th NALSAR–Justice B.R. Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition in Hyderabad on Sunday evening, Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan said the right to vote is part of the Constitution's basic structure and that a process removing millions of citizens from the rolls is intrinsically arbitrary, whatever the justification offered. He stressed notice and hearing before any voter deletion and, in the same address, praised NALSAR students as 'brilliant, bold and brave' amid the recent row over their convocation.
items.why: The remarks come as petitions over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls are being heard in the Supreme Court.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 3 October to 10:00 AM IST, 4 October 2026

items.headline: NHRC takes cognizance of children allegedly used as shields at Mumbai protest
items.text: The Commission issued notices to Mumbai Police, MeitY and X Corp. over reports that minors were brought to a 2 October protest at Shivaji Park and used against police action. It asked for an inquiry into who organised their presence and for FIRs where offences are disclosed.

items.headline: Youth Congress moves Delhi High Court after police refuse Jantar Mantar protest
items.text: Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib has challenged the Delhi Police order of 1 October refusing permission for a protest seeking the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. The plea says the refusal came only on the day of the protest and was disproportionate.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 2 October to 10:00 AM IST, 3 October 2026

items.headline: Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill gets the President's assent
items.text: The President has assented to Gujarat's Uniform Civil Code law. It requires live-in couples to register within a month on pain of up to three months' jail or a fine, fines unregistered marriages and divorces, and treats children of live-in relationships as legitimate.
items.why: Gujarat joins the States with a codified UCC; the date it comes into force is still to be notified.

items.headline: Lawyers' body sets up ex-judges' commission to examine the SIR voter-roll revision
items.text: A commission chaired by former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B. Lokur, with Justices A.K. Patnaik, Badar Durrez Ahmad, Rekha Sharma and Anjana Prakash, will study the legality and impact of the Special Intensive Revision. It plans public hearings across the country and a report by December 2026.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 1 October to 10:00 AM IST, 2 October 2026

items.body: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
items.headline: Indian jurist Bimal N. Patel sworn in as judge of the Law of the Sea tribunal
items.text: Dr Bimal N. Patel, former Director of Gujarat National Law University, took oath in Hamburg as a judge of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea. He was one of five judges inaugurated for the 2026–2035 term.
items.why: India gains a seat on the main international court for maritime disputes.

items.headline: Plea challenges Delhi's 15% deputation and contract route for Additional Public Prosecutors
items.text: Advocate Shipra Mishra has challenged an April 2026 notification that fills 15% of Additional Public Prosecutor posts by deputation or short-term contract. She argues this conflicts with the BNSS, which requires prosecutors from the regular cadre where suitable candidates exist; the High Court has issued notice.

items.headline: Petition in Supreme Court challenges orders mandating all six stanzas of Vande Mataram
items.text: Nagpur-based activist B.D. Borkar has challenged two Union Home Ministry orders of January and July 2026 requiring the full six-stanza Vande Mataram at formal State events. He argues the orders replace the two-stanza version used for decades and violate the rights to equality and free expression.

edition.window: News from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM IST, 1 October 2026

items.headline: Retired judge heading a West Bengal voter-roll appeals tribunal offers to resign over 70-km daily commute
items.text: Former Calcutta High Court judge Justice Indrajit Chatterjee, who heads one of the tribunals hearing appeals from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of West Bengal's electoral rolls, has written to the Chief Justice and the Chief Electoral Officer offering to step down with effect from 2 November. He said the round trip between his home in Salt Lake and the tribunal office at Joka takes about four hours a day, making it impossible to do justice to the work.
items.why: About 7.47 lakh appeals from Murshidabad district are reported to be pending before his tribunal, and he is the second retired judge to leave this work.

items.body: Supreme Court of India / Attorney General
items.headline: Supreme Court asks Attorney General to consider raising the 25-member cap on State Bar Councils
items.text: A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked Attorney General R. Venkataramani to consider a plea to increase the number of elected members in State Bar Councils, which the Advocates Act, 1961 fixes at 25. The Court noted that the profession has grown hugely since 1961 (the Bar Council of Delhi alone has about two lakh advocates) but said changing the number is a policy matter for the Government.
items.why: A larger council size would change how lakhs of advocates are represented, and would interact with the Court's 30% seat quota for women in Bar Councils.

items.headline: Rajanna R elected Chairperson of Karnataka State Bar Council; Shivamurthy is Vice-Chairperson
items.text: Advocate Rajanna R won the Chairperson post with 15 votes, Advocate Shivamurthy was elected Vice-Chairperson with 17 votes, and Advocate Dhananjaya C M was chosen as the Council's member on the Bar Council of India. The electorate included the 23 elected members, two co-opted women members and the Advocate General of Karnataka; the office bearers serve two-year terms.
items.why: The Council was fully constituted this year after an eight-year gap, with five women elected to it for the first time.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 30 September to 10:00 AM IST, 1 October 2026

items.headline: Allahabad High Court judge calls for less Chief Justice-centric administration and more accountability
items.text: In a ruling arising from four cases on delays and bail compliance in the subordinate courts, Justice Vinod Diwakar of the Allahabad High Court questioned how the High Court is run administratively. He noted that about 84 administrative committees are handled by two or three senior judges, that committee minutes are not shared with the Full Court, and that only 16 Full Court meetings were held in ten years even though the rules call for quarterly meetings. He suggested wider participation by puisne judges, clear promotion criteria and accountability mechanisms for administrative decisions.
items.why: It is a rare public critique from within a High Court of how administrative power is concentrated in the Chief Justice and a few senior judges.

items.headline: Orissa High Court lawyers to march to Governor's house and stay away from work over judge vacancies
items.text: The Orissa High Court Bar Association resolved to abstain from court work on 1 October and hold a peaceful march from Bhubaneswar Club to the Governor's residence (Lok Bhawan). It says only 15 of the court's 33 sanctioned judge posts are filled, two more judges retire in November, and over 1.72 lakh cases are pending. The Bar will give the Governor a memorandum for the President seeking quick appointments.
items.why: With the High Court working at under half its sanctioned strength, the Bar is pressing the Centre and the Collegium to fill the vacancies.

edition.window: News from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM IST, 30 September 2026

items.headline: Special bench questions how CAPF contempt case was moved; ASG says she had asked the CJI for joint hearing
items.text: A special bench of Justice Manoj Misra and Justice Ujjal Bhuyan took up the contempt petitions on IPS deputation to the Central Armed Police Forces after they were dropped from Justice Bhuyan's list and reassigned without notice to the petitioners. The bench asked why the original bench was not told before the shift. ASG Aishwarya Bhati said she had mentioned the matter before the Chief Justice to have it heard with the challenge to the CAPF (General Administration) Act, 2026, and apologised for not informing the petitioners. The matter will be heard on 15 October with the writ petitions.
items.why: It raises questions about how cases are listed and moved between benches in the Supreme Court.

items.headline: Karnataka tells High Court it will not act against cinemas over 2% ticket cess for now
items.text: The Karnataka Cine and Cultural Activists (Welfare) Act, under which a 2% cess on cinema ticket revenue is to fund the welfare of cine workers, was due to take effect on 30 September. Responding to challenges by the Multiplex Association of India, PVR INOX and others, the State assured the High Court it would take no coercive action against cinema operators for the time being. The case will be heard next on 26 October.
items.why: Cinema owners in Karnataka get interim protection while the validity of the new cess law is tested.

items.headline: Pension scheme amended so more EPF members earning up to ₹25,000 a month get pension cover
items.text: The Labour Ministry has amended the Employees' Pension Scheme, 2026 by a notification dated 25 September, with effect from 17 September. A new clause lets EPF members earning at or below the new wage ceiling of ₹25,000 a month join the pension scheme even if they were earlier left out.
items.why: It carries the recent rise in the EPF wage ceiling into pension coverage for workers.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 29 September to 10:00 AM IST, 30 September 2026

items.headline: Collegium recommends sending Justice T Vinod Kumar back to Telangana High Court before he retires
items.text: At its meeting on 28 September, the Supreme Court Collegium recommended that Justice T Vinod Kumar, now a judge of the Madras High Court, be repatriated to his parent Telangana High Court. He was appointed to the Telangana High Court in 2019 and moved to Madras in June 2025. The Collegium cited his approaching retirement, due on 16 November 2026.
items.why: If notified by the Centre, he will finish his tenure in his parent High Court.

items.headline: Karnataka High Court sets up 3-judge panel to study new benches in 8 regions
items.text: The Karnataka High Court has formed a committee of Justices Anu Sivaraman, S.G. Pandit and Mohammad Nawaz to examine whether circuit or permanent benches are feasible at Mangaluru, Udupi, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu-Madikeri, Hassan, Davanagere and Uttara Kannada. The panel is to consult stakeholders before reporting. The High Court currently sits at Bengaluru, Dharwad and Kalaburagi.
items.why: The move follows a push from the State for a coastal bench at Mangaluru, which the Advocates' Association Bengaluru has opposed.

items.headline: Supreme Court asks its Registry to explain why a listed contempt case was dropped from the cause list
items.text: A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A.S. Chandurkar found that contempt petitions over IPS deputations to the Central Armed Police Forces had been struck off the day's list around noon, despite a judicial order listing them for 2 pm. The bench directed the Registry to explain the deletion and relisted the matter for 30 September at 2 pm.
items.why: It puts the Supreme Court's own listing process under scrutiny.

items.headline: GNLU students protest over health, water and sanitation problems on campus
items.text: Students at GNLU, Gandhinagar, protested over conditions on campus, citing a student magazine count of 93 dengue cases, 58 cases of an unexplained viral illness and 20 food-poisoning incidents. They demanded independent audits of water, food and sanitation, better medical facilities, and online classes until problems are fixed. The Registrar said water and food tests are under way and bottled water has been supplied.

edition.window: News from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM IST, 29 September 2026

items.headline: RBI shortens deadline for bringing export money home from 15 months to 9 months
items.text: The Reserve Bank of India has amended the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations. Exporters must now realise and repatriate export proceeds within 9 months instead of 15, and within 12 months instead of 18 for exports invoiced in rupees. A new Regulation 20 lets Authorised Dealer banks handle certain older export, import and merchanting transactions without RBI approval. The changes take effect on 1 October 2026.
items.why: Every Indian exporter must adjust payment terms and compliance before the shorter timelines apply from 1 October.

items.headline: JGLS pair win Mediation Championship of India 2026; GNLU student named top mediator
items.text: Omar Sigbathulla and Chinmay Hegde of Jindal Global Law School won the counsel category of the Mediation Championship of India 2026. Ayushi Shukla of Gujarat National Law University won the mediator category. The invitation-only contest, organised by PACT and Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, drew over 100 participants, and the finals were held at the India International Centre, New Delhi.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 28 September to 10:00 AM IST, 29 September 2026

items.headline: Collegium recommends three High Court Chief Justices for elevation to the Supreme Court
items.text: At its meeting on 28 September 2026, the Supreme Court Collegium recommended elevating Justice Sunita Agarwal (Chief Justice, Gujarat High Court), Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya (Chief Justice, Delhi High Court) and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh (Chief Justice, Telangana High Court) as Supreme Court judges. The recommendations now go to the Centre for notification.
items.why: If the Centre clears the names, the Supreme Court gains three judges and the Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana High Courts will each need a new Chief Justice.

items.body: Supreme Court of India / Union Government
items.headline: Supreme Court asks Centre to consider rules on minors' social media accounts; Centre says it will examine
items.text: Hearing a petition by Just Rights for Children Alliance, the Supreme Court asked the Union Government to consider framing statutory rules so that social media platforms follow Indian law on contracts with minors, which treats such contracts as void. The Court pointed to age-verification and parental-consent mechanisms rather than a blanket ban, and the Solicitor General told the Court the Centre would examine the matter.
items.why: It could lead to binding government rules on how children under 18 sign up to and use social media platforms in India.

edition.window: News from 4:00 PM IST, 26 September to 10:00 AM IST, 27 September 2026

items.body: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
items.headline: FSSAI to bring in red-hexagon warning labels on packaged food high in sugar, fat or salt
items.text: FSSAI told the Supreme Court that it will adopt a front-of-pack warning label modelled on Canada's system, a red hexagon, for packaged foods that cross set limits for sugar, fat or salt. It plans to issue and finalise draft regulations in about four months, with a 60-day public consultation and then a 365-day voluntary window for manufacturers. The statement was made in the case 3S and Our Health Society v. Union of India.
items.why: Once notified, the regulations will change food labelling rules for packaged food sold across India.

items.headline: Senior Advocate Dushyant Dave criticises SIR voter-roll revision in memorial lecture
items.text: Delivering the 17th K M Bashir Memorial Lecture on 26 September, Senior Advocate Dushyant Dave said the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls was undermining adult franchise through large-scale deletions of voters in States such as Bihar and West Bengal. He also criticised the delay in the Supreme Court's judgment on the SIR challenge and raised concerns about decision-making within the Election Commission.
items.why: The SIR exercise and its legal challenges remain one of the most debated election-law issues in the country.

edition.window: News from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM IST, 26 September 2026

items.body: Chief Justice of India; Bihar State Legal Services Authority
items.headline: CJI Surya Kant opens a Victim Rights Centre in Patna
items.text: The Chief Justice of India was scheduled to inaugurate a Victim Rights Centre at the Bihar State Legal Services Authority in Patna at 12:10 PM on Saturday. Set up as a pilot under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, the centre gives crime victims one point of contact for legal aid, emergency medical treatment, FIR copies and victim compensation. A transgender helpline is being launched with it, and the pilot will run in Patna district for twelve months before any expansion.
items.why: It tests a single-window model for victim support that could be copied by legal services authorities in other States.

items.headline: CJI holds open house with CNLU Patna students, welcomes idea of court apprenticeship in final year
items.text: At an open-house session with students of Chanakya National Law University in Patna, CJI Surya Kant said the judiciary is committed to protecting students' right to peaceful protest and explained why dissenting views in Collegium deliberations are kept confidential. He called Vice-Chancellor Faizan Mustafa's proposal for a mandatory court apprenticeship in the final year of law studies a welcome new idea, and acknowledged concerns about high fees and too few scholarships. He also pointed to the Sarika Tyagi case on a professional assistance fund for young lawyers, saying such support is a structural need for the profession.
items.why: The CJI's openness to restructuring the law degree may shape future BCI and NLU discussions on legal education.
